words.gloss: shell (śukti), conch (śaṅkha), udra, kumbhīra, culukī, makara and the like
words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva within bahuvrīhi (-ādi)

hindi: कूर्म, कर्कटक, मत्स्य, शिशुमार, तिमिङ्गिल, शुक्ति, शङ्ख, उद्र, कुम्मीर, चुलुकी, मकर आदि —
english: The tortoise (kūrma), the crab (karkaṭaka), the fish (matsya), the śiśumāra, the timiṅgila, the shell (śukti), the conch (śaṅkha), the udra, the kumbhīra, the culukī, the makara and the like —

text_flags.why: possible: there is no stem kummīra; kumbhīra (an aquatic animal) has the same syllable weights, so the metre is unchanged

notes: SENTENCE: the list of water-dwellers (vāriśaya) is closed by 'iti vāriśayāḥ proktāḥ' in 41. Animal names are kept in Sanskrit; plain English words are given only for the ordinary meanings (tortoise, crab, fish, shell, conch). Hindi keeps the printed कुम्मीर.

hindi: इस प्रकार वारिशय कहे गए; वारिचारी कहे जाएँगे — हंस, क्रौञ्च, बलाका, बक, कारण्डव, प्लव,
english: Thus the water-dwellers (vāriśaya) have been told; the water-movers (vāricārin) will be told: the haṃsa, the krauñca, the balākā, the baka, the kāraṇḍava, the plava,
notes: SENTENCE: the list of water-movers runs on to 44. Bird names are kept in Sanskrit, without identification.

hindi: शरारि, पुष्कराह्व, केशरी, मणितुण्डक, मृणालकण्ठ, मद्गु, कादम्ब, काकतुण्डक,
english: the śarāri, the puṣkarāhva, the keśarin, the maṇituṇḍaka, the mṛṇālakaṇṭha, the madgu, the kādamba, the kākatuṇḍaka,
notes: List of water-movers (vāricārin) continued from 41. Literal senses of compound names are given only in the glosses.

hindi: उत्क्रोश, पुण्डरीकाक्ष, मेघराव, अम्बुकुक्कुटी, आरा, नन्दीमुखी, वाटी, सुमुख, सहचारी,
english: the utkrośa, the puṇḍarīkākṣa, the megharāva, the ambukukkuṭī, the ārā, the nandīmukhī, the vāṭī, the sumukhas, the sahacārins,
notes: List of water-movers continued. sumukhāḥ and sahacāriṇaḥ are plural; they are taken as two bird names, but 'the fair-faced ones that move together (in flocks)', one description, is also possible.

hindi: रोहिणी, कामकाली, सारस, रक्तशीर्षक, चक्रवाक, और इसी प्रकार अन्य जलचारी पक्षी हैं।
english: the rohiṇī, the kāmakālī, the sārasa, the raktaśīrṣaka, the cakravāka; and likewise there are other birds that move in water.
notes: raktaśīrṣakaḥ is taken as a separate name; it may also be an epithet of the sārasa ('the red-headed sārasa').

hindi: पृषत, शरभ, राम, श्वदंष्ट्र, मृगमातृका, शश और उरण, कुरङ्ग, गोकर्ण, कोट्टकारक,
english: The pṛṣata, the śarabha, the rāma, the śvadaṃṣṭra, the mṛgamātṛkā, the hare (śaśa) and the uraṇa, the kuraṅga, the gokarṇa, the koṭṭakāraka,
notes: SENTENCE: the list of dry-land animals (jāṅgala mṛga) is closed in 46. Names kept in Sanskrit, without identification; glosses 'deer' or 'animal' are only general. koṭṭakāraka is left unsplit.

hindi: चारुष्क, हरिण और एण, शम्बर, कालपुच्छक, ऋष्य और वरपोत — ये जाङ्गल मृग जानने चाहिए।
english: the cāruṣka, the hariṇa and the eṇa, the śambara, the kālapucchaka, the ṛṣya and the varapota are to be known as the dry-land animals (jāṅgala mṛga).
notes: mṛga here is the general word for the wild animals of the group. varapota is left unsplit.

hindi: लाव, वर्तीरक, वार्तीक कपिञ्जल के साथ, चकोर, उपचक्र, कुक्कुभ, रक्तवर्त्मक —
english: The lāva, the vartīraka, the vārtīka together with the kapiñjala, the cakora, the upacakra, the kukkubha, the raktavartmaka —
notes: SENTENCE: closed in 48 'lāvādyā viṣkirās tv ete'. sakapiñjalaḥ 'with the kapiñjala' adds the kapiñjala to the list. eva after ca is not rendered separately.

hindi: ये लाव आदि विष्किर हैं; वर्तक आदि कहे जाएँगे — वर्तक, वर्तिका, बर्ही, तित्तिरि और कुक्कुट,
english: These, beginning with the lāva, are scatterers (viṣkira); those beginning with the vartaka will be told: the vartaka, the vartikā, the peacock (barhin), the tittiri and the cock (kukkuṭa),
notes: tu is left untranslated (connective). The second viṣkira list runs on to 49.

hindi: कङ्क, शारपद, इन्द्राभ, गोनर्द, गिरिवर्तक, क्रकर, अवकर और वारड — ये विष्किर हैं।
english: the kaṅka, the śārapada, the indrābha, the gonarda, the girivartaka, the krakara, the avakara and the vāraḍa: these are the scatterers (viṣkira).
notes: The members of the long compound are bird names; girivartaka ('mountain vartaka') and indrābha are kept as single names.

hindi: शतपत्र, भृङ्गराज, कोयष्टि, जीवजीवक, कैरात, कोकिल, अत्यूह, गोपापुत्र, प्रियात्मज,
english: The śatapatra, the bhṛṅgarāja, the koyaṣṭi, the jīvajīvaka, the kairāta, the kokila, the atyūha, the gopāputra, the priyātmaja,
notes: SENTENCE: the list of peckers (pratuda) runs on to 53, where it is closed. Names kept in Sanskrit, without identification; plant senses of śatapatra and bhṛṅgarāja do not apply here.

words.gloss: laṭṭaṣaka (a bird) (variant: with ṭū for ṭa)

hindi: लट्टा, लट्टषक, बभ्रु, वटहा, डिण्डिमानक, जटी, दुन्दुभि, पाक्कार, लोहपृष्ठ, कुलिङ्गक,
english: the laṭṭā, the laṭṭaṣaka, the babhru, the vaṭahā, the ḍiṇḍimānaka, the jaṭin, the dundubhi, the pākkāra, the lohapṛṣṭha ('iron-back'), the kuliṅgaka,
notes: Pratuda list continued. 'laṭṭa(ṭū)ṣako' prints the syllable ṭū in round brackets as the edition's alternative (apparently laṭūṣaka or laṭṭūṣaka; its exact extent is not clear); the unbracketed reading laṭṭaṣaka is used and the variant is left out of the translations. vaṭahā is taken as a feminine name; its form is uncertain. ḍiṇḍimānaka and pākkāra are left unsplit.

hindi: कपोत, शुक, शारङ्ग, चिरटी, कङ्कुयष्टिका, सारिका, कलविङ्क, चटक, अङ्गारचूडक,
english: the pigeon (kapota), the parrot (śuka), the śāraṅga, the ciraṭī, the kaṅkuyaṣṭikā, the sārikā, the kalaviṅka, the sparrow (caṭaka), the aṅgāracūḍaka,
notes: Pratuda list continued. ciraṭīkaṅkuyaṣṭikāḥ is divided as ciraṭī + kaṅkuyaṣṭikā; a division into three names (ciraṭī, kaṅku, yaṣṭikā) is also possible.

hindi: पारावत, पाण्डविक — ये प्रतुद पक्षी कहे गए। बलपूर्वक पकड़कर खाते हैं, इसलिए वे प्रसह नाम वाले हैं।
english: the pārāvata and the pāṇḍavika: these are told to be the pecking birds (pratuda). Because they eat seizing by force, they are therefore named seizers (prasaha).
notes: 'pāṇḍa(na)vikaḥ' prints na in round brackets as the edition's alternative (apparently pānavika or pāṇḍanavika; its extent is not clear); the unbracketed reading pāṇḍavika is used and the variant is left out of the translations. dvija 'twice-born' is a common word for bird. Line b begins the explanation of the group names, continued in 54-55; it explains the name prasaha.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., aluk upapada tat-puruṣa

hindi: बिल में रहने के कारण भूशय, अनूप का आश्रय लेने के कारण आनूप, जल में निवास के कारण जलज, और जल में विचरण के कारण जलेचर (कहलाते हैं)।
english: From dwelling in burrows (they are called) ground-dwellers (bhūśaya); from resorting to marshland (anūpa), marsh animals (ānūpa); from dwelling in water, water-born (jalaja); from moving in water, water-movers (jalecara).
notes: jalaja here answers to the vārija/vāriśaya group and jalecara to the vāricārin group named in 41 and 56. jalecaryāt is read as the ablative of a neuter jalecarya 'moving in water'; the gender of the abstract is uncertain. The words 'are called' are understood.

hindi: स्थल पर उत्पन्न, जाङ्गल में विचरने वाले मृग जाङ्गल कहे गए हैं; बिखेरने से विष्किर, और चोंच मारने से प्रतुद माने गए हैं।
english: The animals born on dry land and moving in dry country are called dry-land (jāṅgala); from scattering, scatterers (viṣkira); from pecking, peckers (pratuda): so they are known.
notes: The absolutives vikīrya and pratudya are rendered 'from scattering', 'from pecking'. iti closes the explanation; it is rendered by 'so'.

hindi: मांसों की यह योनि आठ प्रकार की कही गई है। प्रसह, भूशय, आनूप, वारिज और वारिचारी —
english: This source (yoni) of meats is declared to be eightfold. The seizers (prasaha), ground-dwellers (bhūśaya), marsh animals (ānūpa), water-born (vārija) and water-movers (vāricārin) —
notes: SENTENCE: line b begins a sentence that runs through 57-59a (their qualities and use); the other three groups (viṣkira, pratuda, jāṅgala) are named in 59b. vārija here is the group called vāriśaya in 41 and jalaja in 54.

hindi: — भारी, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, मधुर, बल और उपचय को बढ़ाने वाले, वृष्य, अत्यन्त वातहर और कफ-पित्त को बढ़ाने वाले हैं।
english: are heavy, hot, unctuous and sweet, increasing strength and increase of body (upacaya), aphrodisiac, supremely Vāta-removing and increasing Kapha and Pitta.
notes: param is taken with vātaharāḥ; it may also go with the preceding vṛṣyāḥ ('supremely aphrodisiac'). The subject is the five groups named in 56b.

hindi: वे नित्य व्यायाम करने वालों के लिए और जो मनुष्य दीप्त अग्नि वाले हैं (उनके लिए) हितकर हैं। वैद्य विशेष रूप से मांसाहारी प्रसहों का मांस —
english: They are wholesome for those constantly exercising and for men who have a kindled digestive fire (agni). The physician should apply especially the meat of the seizers (prasaha), which eat meat,
notes: narāḥ ... ye is nominative where the dative of the line's first half is expected ('and the men who have kindled digestive fire'); it is translated in the dative sense. Line b continues into 59a (prayojayet). 'should apply' is the verb of 59a.

words.gloss: for those afflicted with chronic arśas, grahaṇī disorder and śoṣa
words.gram: m. gen. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: — पुराने अर्श, ग्रहणीदोष और शोष से पीड़ितों के लिए प्रयोग करे। लाव आदि विष्किर-वर्ग, प्रतुद और जाङ्गल मृग —
english: for those afflicted with chronic arśas, grahaṇī disorder and śoṣa (wasting). The scatterers' group (viṣkira) beginning with the lāva, the peckers (pratuda) and the dry-land animals (jāṅgala mṛga) —
notes: jīrṇa 'chronic, old' is taken with arśas only; it may qualify all three disorders. arśas, grahaṇī and śoṣa are kept as Sanskrit. SENTENCE: line b begins a sentence completed in 60.

hindi: — लघु, शीत, मधुर, कषाय-युक्त, और उस सन्निपात में मनुष्यों के लिए हितकर हैं जिसमें पित्त प्रधान, वात मध्यम और कफ अनुगामी हो।
english: are light, cold and sweet, with astringent taste, and wholesome for men in a sannipāta (all three doṣas combined) in which Pitta is uppermost, Vāta in the middle and Kapha following.
notes: kaphānuge 'with Kapha following' is taken as Kapha being least.

hindi: परन्तु वर्तक आदि विष्किर गुणों में प्रसहों से थोड़ा अन्तर रखते हैं। बकरे का मांस न अधिक शीत, न भारी, न स्निग्ध है, दोष न बढ़ाने वाला —
english: But the scatterers (viṣkira) beginning with the vartaka differ little from the seizers (prasaha) in qualities. Goat meat (āja) is not too cold, heavy or unctuous, and does not produce doṣas;
notes: Line b begins a description of goat meat continued in 62a. na ati- is taken with all three adjectives. doṣala 'producing doṣa' with the negative a-.

words.gloss: from sameness with the body's dhātus

hindi: शरीर की धातुओं से समानता के कारण वह अनभिष्यन्दी और बृंहण है। भेड़ का मांस मधुर और शीत होने से भारी और बृंहण है।
english: from its sameness (sāmānya) with the body's dhātus it is not channel-clogging and is nourishing. Sheep meat (āvika), being sweet and cold, is heavy and nourishing.
notes: Line a completes the description of goat meat begun in 61b.

hindi: बकरे और भेड़ के विषय में, मिश्रित विचरण-क्षेत्र होने से, योनि अनिश्चित है। सामान्य रूप से बताए गए मांसों में से, अपने-अपने गुणों के अनुसार अलग-अलग —
english: In goat and sheep the source (yoni) is undetermined, since they have a mixed range. Of the meats taught in general, separately by their own qualities,
notes: yonau ... aniścite is read as a locative absolute ('the source being undetermined'), with ajāvike as a neuter samāhāra locative; yoni is construed here as masculine (loc. yonau with aniścite). The point is that goat and sheep are not placed in any of the eight groups. Line b continues into 64a.

words.gloss: for sight, hearing, intellect, digestive fire, age, complexion, voice and life-span

hindi: कुछ का, गुणों की विशेषता के कारण, विशेष (वर्णन) बताया जाएगा। दृष्टि, श्रवण, मेधा, अग्नि, वय, वर्ण, स्वर और आयु के लिए —
english: the particulars of some will be taught, owing to the distinctiveness of their qualities. For sight, hearing, intellect, digestive fire (agni), age (vayas), complexion, voice and life-span —
notes: viśeṣa upadekṣyate: visarga dropped before u (hiatus), 16 syllables. Line b is governed by hitatamaḥ in 65a. vayas 'age' may mean youthfulness here; kept literal.

hindi: — मोर अत्यन्त हितकर है; वह बलकारक, वातनाशक और मांस तथा शुक्र को बढ़ाने वाला है। भारी, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, मधुर, स्वर, वर्ण और बल देने वाले —
english: the peacock (barhin) is most beneficial; it is strengthening, Vāta-destroying and promotes flesh and semen. Heavy, hot, unctuous and sweet, giving voice, complexion and strength,
notes: Line b begins the description of the haṃsas completed in 66a.

hindi: — बृंहण, शुक्रकारक और मारुत का नाश करने वाले हंस कहे गए हैं। स्निग्ध, उष्ण, वृष्य, बृंहण, स्वर को जगाने वाले —
english: nourishing and semen-promoting, destroying Vāta (māruta), are said to be the haṃsas. Unctuous, hot, aphrodisiac, nourishing, awakening the voice,
notes: Line a completes the haṃsa description begun in 65b. Line b begins the description of the caraṇāyudhas completed in 67a.

words.gloss: from frequenting dry land and marshland
words.gram: n. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: — बलकारक, अत्यन्त वातहर और स्वेद लाने वाले चरणायुध हैं। भारी, उष्ण, मधुर, और धन्व तथा अनूप का अधिक सेवन न करने के कारण —
english: strengthening, supremely Vāta-removing and causing sweat are the caraṇāyudhas ('foot-weaponed', that is cocks). Heavy, hot and sweet, from not frequenting dry land (dhanvan) and marshland (anūpa) excessively,
notes: caraṇāyudha 'having feet as weapons' is an ordinary word for the cock. param may also go with balyāḥ ('supremely strengthening'). Line b begins the tittiri description completed in 68a; na ati- is taken as 'not too much' with niṣevaṇa.

words.gloss: in disorders of Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman)
words.gram: m. loc. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: — तित्तिरि अनिल-प्रधान तीनों दोषों को शीघ्र जीत लेता है। रक्त-सहित पित्त और श्लेष्मा के विकारों में कपिञ्जल —
english: the tittiri quickly overcomes the three doṣas when Vāta (anila) is predominant. In disorders of Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman) involving blood, the kapiñjalas —
notes: saṃjayet is an optative of general statement, rendered as a present. Line b runs into 69a (śasyante).

words.gloss: because of coldness, sweetness and lightness

hindi: — (और) मन्द वात वालों में शीतलता, मधुरता और लघुता के कारण प्रशस्त हैं। लाव कषाय-मधुर, लघु, अग्नि को बढ़ाने वाले —
english: (and) in those with mild Vāta are praised, because of their coldness, sweetness and lightness. The lāvas are astringent and sweet, light, increasing the digestive fire (agni),
notes: mandavāteṣu may refer to disorders or to persons with mild Vāta. The bracketed 'and' joins the two locatives; it is not printed. Line b runs into 70a.

hindi: — सन्निपात को शान्त करने वाले और विपाक में कटु हैं। गोधा विपाक में मधुर, रस में कषाय-कटु —
english: allaying sannipāta, and pungent in vipāka (post-digestive effect). The godhā is sweet in vipāka and astringent and pungent in taste,
notes: Line b runs into 71a. godhā kept as Sanskrit, without identification.

hindi: — वात-पित्त को शान्त करने वाली, बृंहण और बल बढ़ाने वाली है। शल्लक मधुर-अम्ल और विपाक में कटु माना गया है;
english: allaying Vāta and Pitta, nourishing and increasing strength. The śallaka is sweet and sour, and is held to be pungent in vipāka;
notes: Line a completes the godhā (feminine forms). śallaka kept as Sanskrit, without identification. Line b continues into 72a.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: वह वात, पित्त और कफ का नाश करने वाला तथा कास और श्वास को हरने वाला है। कषाय, विशद, शीत, रक्तपित्त को दूर करने वाले —
english: it destroys Vāta, Pitta and Kapha, and likewise removes cough (kāsa) and dyspnoea (śvāsa). Astringent, non-slimy, cold, removing raktapitta,
notes: Line b begins the description of house pigeons completed in 73a.

hindi: — और विपाक में मधुर घर में रहने वाले कपोत हैं। उनसे कुछ हल्के वन में रहने वाले कपोत हैं;
english: and sweet in vipāka are the house-dwelling pigeons (kapota). Somewhat lighter than those are the forest-dwelling pigeons;
notes: ca eva is rendered by 'and' only. Line b continues into 74a.

hindi: वे शीत, संग्राही और बहुत कम मूत्र करने वाले हैं। शुक का मांस कषाय-अम्ल, विपाक में रूक्ष और शीतल —
english: they are cold, binding, and cause very scanty urine. Parrot (śuka) meat is astringent and sour, and in vipāka dry and cold,
notes: vipāke is taken with rūkṣaśītalam, following the word order; it may also go with kaṣāyāmlam ('astringent and sour in vipāka'). Line b runs into 75a.

words.gloss: wholesome in śoṣa, cough and kṣaya
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: — शोष, कास और क्षय में हितकर, संग्राही, लघु और दीपन है। चटक मधुर, स्निग्ध, बल और शुक्र को बढ़ाने वाले —
english: wholesome in śoṣa (wasting), cough and kṣaya (depletion), binding, light and stimulating digestion. Sparrows (caṭaka) are sweet, unctuous, increasing strength and semen,
notes: śoṣa and kṣaya are kept as Sanskrit with literal glosses only. Line b runs into 76a.

hindi: — सन्निपात को शान्त करने वाले और मारुत का शमन करने वाले हैं। कषाय, विशद, रूक्ष, शीत, पाक में कटु, लघु —
english: allaying sannipāta and pacifying Vāta (māruta). Astringent, non-slimy, dry, cold, pungent in vipāka (pāka), light,
notes: Line b begins the description of the hare completed in 77a.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvigu first member)

hindi: — शश मधुर है और उस सन्निपात में प्रशस्त है जिसमें अनिल सबसे कम हो। मधुर, पाक में मधुर, त्रिदोष को शान्त करने वाले, कल्याणकारी —
english: is the hare (śaśa); it is sweet and is praised in a sannipāta in which Vāta (anila) is lowest. Sweet, sweet in vipāka, pacifying the three doṣas, beneficial,
notes: śaśa is said to be both kaṣāya (76b) and svādu 'sweet'; both are kept as printed. Line b begins the description of the eṇas completed in 78a.

hindi: — लघु, मल-मूत्र को बाँधने वाले और शीत एण कहे गए हैं। स्नेहन, बृंहण, वृष्य, श्रम का नाश करने वाला, अनिल को दूर करने वाला —
english: light, binding faeces and urine, and cold are declared to be the eṇas. Oleating (snehana), nourishing, aphrodisiac, destroying fatigue (śrama), removing Vāta (anila),
notes: baddhaviṇmūtra is literally 'having faeces and urine bound', rendered as 'binding faeces and urine'. Line b begins the description of boar meat completed in 79a.

hindi: — वराह का मांस बलकारक, रुचिकारक, स्वेद लाने वाला और भारी है। गाय का (मांस) केवल वात के (विकारों) में, पीनस में, विषमज्वर में —
english: is boar (varāha) meat; it is strengthening, appetizing, causing sweat and heavy. Beef (gavya) in (disorders) of Vāta alone, in pīnasa, in irregular fever (viṣamajvara),
notes: SENTENCE: line b continues into the next unit (outside this chunk), where the use of beef is completed. kevalavāteṣu 'in those of Vāta alone' (bahuvrīhi, without another doṣa); the noun (disorders or persons) is understood. gavya 'belonging to the cow' with 'meat' understood.
